# Sammappadhānavibhaṅga (Vb 8)

**ID:** Vb 8  
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Sammappadhānavibhaṅga

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* is the eighth book or chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text is devoted to an analytical exposition of the four right strivings (*sammappadhāna*): the exertion to prevent unarisen unwholesome states, to abandon arisen unwholesome states, to arouse unarisen wholesome states, and to maintain and develop arisen wholesome states [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its exposition includes a Suttanta analysis (*suttantabhājaniya*) providing the standard formula from the discourses followed by word-by-word definitions of its constituent terms [Nyanatiloka 2007; Gethin 2001]. In these definitions, the terms *vāyamati* ("strives"), *viriya* ("energy"), and *padahati* ("exerts") are explicated in identical terms that correspond to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* register for *viriya*, while *chanda* is glossed as *kattukamyatā* ("desire to act"), representing its earliest formal Abhidhamma definition [Gethin 2001]. Later commentarial exegesis on the chapter is preserved in the *Sammohavinodanī* (*Vibh-a* 291–292) [Gethin 2001].

**Sources**

- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, rev. 2007) — Description of the four right efforts and the Sutta-explanation (suttantabhājaniya).
- [Gethin 2001] R. M. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiya Dhamma (2001) — Analysis of the definitions of vāyamati, viriya, padahati, and chanda in the text, and citation of its commentary (Vibh-a).
